features.feature_value: Kept/considered keeping based on the idea that to have one side heard, the other side must also be heard; only removed truly dangerous items.
features.evidence_span: "if I wanted my opinion's side to be heard the other side had to be heard as well"
features.rationale: The participant frames their decision around balancing hearing both sides, indicating the pair helped them justify non-removal except for danger.

features.feature_value: Removed posts with profanity or direct insults; kept posts that were logical arguments.
features.evidence_span: "Removed anything that included profanity or direct insults.  Kept things that were logical arguments."
features.rationale: They explicitly state content-based criteria linking language (profanity/insults) to removal and reasoning to keeping.

features.feature_value: Removed content perceived as a threat to the US/people/groups and removed messages using vulgar language to make political points.
features.evidence_span: "removed any of them if the message could be taken as a threat to the US"
features.rationale: Their criteria emphasize threat cues and vulgar language as grounds for removal.

features.feature_value: Would keep both if at least one advances conversation; dislikes arguing/insulting between people.
features.evidence_span: "I would keep both posts if at least one of them was moving the conversation forward"
features.rationale: They provide a decision rule prioritizing conversational progress over hostility.

features.feature_value: Belief that aggressive approach and language are not needed to express opinions.
features.evidence_span: "Aggressive approach and language are not needed to express opinions"
features.rationale: This reflects a normative principle against aggression shaping keep/remove beyond specific thresholds.

features.feature_value: Kept posts that expressed opinions with supporting reasoning; removed rude/hurtful content lacking real claims, regardless of being longer.
features.evidence_span: "Others were just being rude and hurtful... without any real claims"
features.rationale: They distinguish substantive reasoning from mere rudeness and note that length alone doesn’t matter.

features.feature_value: Used both versions to compare treatment more fairly, focusing on whether posts were harmful to political discussion; tolerated harsh/sarcastic tone unless direct threats/targeted serious harassment.
features.evidence_span: "Seeing both versions helped me compare them more fairly"
features.rationale: The participant explicitly says the paired exposure enabled a fairer comparison of tone and context, influencing what they allowed.

features.feature_value: Chose 'intelligent ones' characterized by a healthy debate and no cussing.
features.rationale: They connect profanity avoidance to perceived intelligence/quality, indicating a cue-driven keep preference.
